text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
- Helsinki city environmental committee proposes ban on private cars and free public transport to avert serious air pollution.
- Pupils of selected schools in the Helsinki area to take part in experiment aimed at eradicating racist prejudice.
- New St Petersburg governor Vladimir Jakovlev arrives in Helsinki for two-day vist. @
- Drunken Finn delays Tallinn-Helsinki flight with joke of bomb threat.
- Reliable European Commission source says commission will on Wednesday reject Kesko's Tuko acquisition and give Kesko six months to sell Tuko.
- Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS) will increase operations in Finland by opening new Tampere-Stockholm route in March, and adding eight new daily flights to Finland. @

- Danish Unibank ups forecast for Finnish 1997 GDP growth to 4.0 percent from 3.0 percent and forecasts that Bank of Finland will gradually raise short interest rates in 1997. Sees three-month Helibor rate up to 3.25 percent early 1997 and to 3.75 percent late next year.
- Finance minister Sauli Niinisto rebuffs trade unions' proposal of buffer funds as a condition for Finland joining EMU.
- Central Union of Agricultural Producers (MTK) chairman Esa Harmala says study should be made on effects of EMU on investment and job creation. @
- Iraqi Kurd asylum seeker on seventh-day of hunger strike to draw attention to plight in Finland of asylum seekers whose applications may sometimes take years to process.
